mainTopic: A delayed baby (משתהה); the signs of a סריס and an אילונית; reading the משנה about the סריס
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining a source about an eight-month baby. If the baby's hair and nails are fully grown, רבי holds he may really be a seven-month baby who was simply delayed in the womb (משתהה). It then asks how רבא תוספאה could rule that a baby born twelve months after the husband left is legitimate, since that seems to follow רבי alone. The answer is that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees, so the ruling follows more than one sage. Next, a ברייתא defines a סריס חמה and an אילונית as someone who reaches twenty without two hairs, and lists many physical signs for each. רב הונא says all the signs are needed, while רבי יוחנן says one is enough. The גמרא limits their argument to a man without beard hairs and uses this to explain the story of רבה בר אבוה checking רב נחמן. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה. It shows that the משנה's סריס is one born that way, following רבי עקיבא, and it begins reading the line about a סריס who did חליצה. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the quoted source about the eight-month baby
steps.stepSummary: These words finish a source quoted just before this section. It said a mother may lean over and nurse an eight-month baby because of danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: …because of the danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a source it brought up as a challenge right before this section. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source lets the mother nurse the baby because of danger. That suggests the baby might actually be viable. The גמרא now has to explain how this fits with the rule that an eight-month baby is not viable.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born in the eighth month, treated as not viable

phrases.english: because of the danger.
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of the source quoted just before, which let the mother nurse an eight-month baby.

steps.kashyaTarget: The rule about eight-month babies and whether a baby can be delayed in the womb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Talking about danger to the baby suggests a viable child, even though the source calls it an eight-month baby.

steps.title: The source is talking about a baby whose signs are fully developed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the source is dealing with a baby whose signs of full development are complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where his signs are fully developed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case. The source is talking about a baby who looks fully developed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the baby's signs are complete, he may really be a viable baby. That explains the concern for danger. The next step brings a ברייתא to show what these signs are.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? A standard way of narrowing a case
Signs, here physical signs of full development

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
Where his signs are fully developed.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source seemed to treat every eighth-month birth the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source is dealing with a baby whose signs of development are complete.

steps.title: ברייתא: what makes a baby a בן שמונה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines a בן שמונה as a baby whose months were not completed. רבי says the proof is hair and nails that are not fully grown.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Who is a בן שמונה? Anyone whose months were not completed. רבי says: signs prove it about him, namely his hair and nails that are not fully grown.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that physical signs decide whether a baby counts as a בן שמונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion goes by the months of pregnancy. רבי says we look at the baby's body instead: hair and nails that are not fully grown show he is a בן שמונה.

keyTerms.meaning: His months of pregnancy were completed

phrases.english: As it is taught: Who is an eight-month baby?
Anyone whose months were not completed.
רבי says: signs prove it about him,
his hair and his nails that are not fully grown.

steps.raayaObject: That fully developed signs matter for deciding a baby's status

steps.title: Inference: complete signs mean a delayed seven-month baby
steps.stepSummary: From רבי's words the גמרא infers that a baby with complete hair and nails is a seven-month baby who was simply delayed in the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he is a בן שמונה is that his hair and nails are not fully grown. But if they are fully grown, we say this is a seven-month baby who was just delayed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads between the lines of רבי's statement. If incomplete signs make a בן שמונה, then complete signs show something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hair and nails are complete, the baby was ready at seven months and just stayed in longer. Such a baby is viable. This is the idea of משתהה, that a baby can be delayed in the womb.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is… (used to start a precise inference)
A seven-month baby, who is viable
He was simply delayed (in the womb)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, a baby with complete hair and nails is viewed as a viable seven-month baby who stayed longer in the womb (משתהה).

phrases.english: The reason is that they are not fully grown.
But if they are fully grown, we say
this is a seven-month baby,
and he was simply delayed.

steps.raayaObject: A fully developed baby can be delayed in the womb
steps.raayaSupportSource: Inference from רבי's statement in the ברייתא

steps.title: רבא תוספאה's ruling seems to follow רבי alone
steps.stepSummary: רבא תוספאה ruled that a baby born twelve months after the husband went overseas is legitimate. The גמרא asks whose view that follows and answers that it must be רבי's.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, the case where רבא תוספאה ruled about a woman whose husband went overseas, and the baby was delayed for twelve months, and he declared the child fit: whose view is this? רבי's, who says a baby can be delayed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges a real ruling. It seems to rely only on רבי, who is a single opinion against the first view in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Declaring the child legitimate means assuming he stayed in the womb a very long time. Only רבי clearly holds that a baby can be delayed. Usually we do not rule like one sage against the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: A later אמורא who gave the ruling
A real case, a practical ruling
He declared him fit (legitimate, not a ממזר)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether רבי holds a baby can be delayed. He does. The question is how a practical ruling could follow one sage against the others.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָא דַּעֲבַד רָבָא תּוֹסְפָאָה עוֹבָדָא
phrases.english: But this case where רבא תוספאה gave a practical ruling
about a woman whose husband went overseas
and it was delayed up to the twelve months of the year,
phrases.notes: "It" is the baby. It was born twelve months after the husband left.

phrases.english: and he declared him fit.
According to whom? According to רבי, who says it can be delayed!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דַּעֲבַד רָבָא תּוֹסְפָאָה עוֹבָדָא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא תוספאה's ruling that the child was legitimate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling depends on משתהה, which seems to be only רבי's view against the others. A practical ruling should not follow a lone opinion.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees, so it is not a lone view
steps.stepSummary: Since רבן שמעון בן גמליאל also holds that a baby can be delayed, רבא תוספאה was not following a lone opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is also רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says a baby can be delayed, רבא תוספאה acted like the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by finding another sage who agrees with רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two major sages holding משתהה, רבי is no longer a lone voice. That makes it reasonable to rely on this view in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: He acted like the majority, not like a lone opinion

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Since there is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
who says it can be delayed,
he acted like the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא תוספאה seemed to follow רבי alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees, so the ruling follows a stronger, shared view.

steps.title: Source: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on surviving thirty days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view: any baby who lives thirty days is not a נפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: any human baby who lives thirty days is not a נפל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source proving that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds a baby can be delayed in the womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a baby born early is treated as viable if he survives thirty days. This shows he was really a full baby who was delayed. So רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees with the idea of משתהה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא תוספאה's ruling stands because both רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל accept that a baby can be delayed in the womb.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
Any human baby who lived thirty days
is not a non-viable baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.raayaObject: That רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds a baby can be delayed
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about thirty days

steps.title: Definition of a סריס חמה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines a סריס חמה as a man who reaches twenty without growing two hairs. He stays in that status even if hairs grow later.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Who is a סריס חמה? Anyone who is twenty and has not grown two hairs. Even if he grows them afterward, he is like a סריס in all his matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: who counts as a סריס חמה, a man who is naturally a eunuch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Age twenty without two hairs fixes his status. Later growth does not change it. He is treated as a סריס for all laws.

keyTerms.meaning: A eunuch by natural causes, born that way
Two hairs, the sign of physical maturity
For all his matters, in every law

phrases.english: The רבנן taught: Who is a natural eunuch?
phrases.notes: Literally "a eunuch of the sun." It means a man who was born this way.

phrases.english: Anyone who is twenty years old
and has not grown two hairs.
And even if he grew them after this,
he is like a eunuch in all his matters.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Twenty years old without two hairs makes him a סריס חמה, even if hairs grow later.

steps.title: The physical signs of a סריס חמה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists his signs: no beard, defective hair, and smooth skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are his signs: anyone who has no beard, whose hair is defective, and whose skin is smooth.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives the signs that identify a סריס חמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides the missing two hairs at twenty, the ברייתא gives visible body signs. These help identify the condition.

phrases.english: And these are his signs:
anyone who has no beard,
and his hair is defective,
and his skin is smooth.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The signs are no beard, defective hair, and smooth skin.

steps.title: Another sign: urine that does not foam
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, in the name of רבי יהודה בן יאיר, gives another sign: his urine does not foam.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי יהודה בן יאיר: anyone whose urine does not raise foam.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא adds a different sign for a סריס חמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of looking at hair or skin, this opinion gives a sign about the body's function: his urine does not foam.
steps.whatToRemember: A סריס חמה is set by age twenty without two hairs. The ברייתא gives body signs (no beard, defective hair, smooth skin), and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds urine that does not foam.

phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says
in the name of רבי יהודה בן יאיר:
anyone whose urine does not raise foam.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן יָאִיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sign of a סריס חמה is that his urine does not foam.

steps.title: Three more opinions on the signs of a סריס
steps.stepSummary: Three יש אומרים opinions add signs of a סריס חמה: his urine forms no arch, his semen is watery, and his urine does not ferment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: a סריס is anyone who urinates without making an arch. Some say: anyone whose semen is watery. Some say: anyone whose urine does not ferment.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps listing signs of a סריס חמה. Here it adds three more opinions, each introduced by 'some say'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion gives a physical sign showing the man's body did not develop normally. These signs are added to the list from Steps 9 and 10. Each one is the view of a different unnamed תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Some say', an unnamed opinion in the ברייתא
An arch, the curved stream of normal urination

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 10. There, רבי יהודה בן יאיר said the urine does not foam. Here, a different opinion says the urine does not ferment. These are two separate signs.

phrases.english: And some say: anyone who urinates
and does not form an arch.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: כֹּל שֶׁשִּׁכְבַת זַרְעוֹ דּוֹחָה.
phrases.english: And some say: anyone whose semen is watery.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין מֵימֵי רַגְלָיו מַחְמִיצִין.
phrases.english: And some say: anyone whose urine does not ferment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: כׇּל הַמֵּטִיל מַיִם וְאֵין עוֹשֶׂה כִּיפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of signs of a סריס חמה from Steps 9 and 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Further signs of a סריס: urine without an arch, watery semen, and urine that does not ferment.

steps.title: Last two signs of a סריס: no steam and an unclear voice
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say a סריס gives off no steam when he bathes in winter. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says his voice is defective, so you cannot tell whether he is a man or a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: anyone who bathes in the rainy season and his body does not give off steam. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: anyone whose voice is defective, so you cannot tell if he is a man or a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list of signs of a סריס with two more opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are two more separate opinions on how to spot a סריס. One looks for steam from the body after bathing in winter, and the other looks at whether the voice is clearly a man's. The steam sign matters later, in the story of רב נחמן in Step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a name for a specific unnamed תנא
Steam or vapor rising from the body

steps.whyThisMatters: The steam sign is exactly what רבה בר אבוה later tells the רבנן to check on רב נחמן.

phrases.aramaic: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: כֹּל שֶׁרוֹחֵץ בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים
phrases.english: Others say: anyone who bathes in the rainy season
and his flesh does not give off steam.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
anyone whose voice is defective,
so that one cannot tell whether he is a man or a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: כֹּל שֶׁרוֹחֵץ בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of signs of a סריס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סריס may also be recognized by giving off no steam when bathing in winter, or by a voice that is not clearly male.

steps.title: Who counts as an אילונית
steps.stepSummary: An אילונית is a woman who reaches twenty without growing two hairs. Even if hairs grow later, she stays an אילונית in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is an אילונית? Any woman who is twenty years old and has not grown two hairs. Even if she grows them afterward, she is still an אילונית in all her matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now turns from the male case, the סריס, to the matching female case, the אילונית, and defines her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definition matches the סריס definition from Step 8 exactly. The test is reaching twenty without two hairs, and growing hairs later does not change her status.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose body did not develop sexually and who cannot have children
Two hairs, the basic sign of physical maturity
In all her matters, meaning for every halachic purpose

phrases.english: And who is an aylonit?
Any woman who is twenty years old
and has not grown two hairs,
and even if she grows them afterward,
she is like an aylonit in all her matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the male case, the סריס, to the parallel female case, the אילונית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who reaches twenty without two hairs is an אילונית, even if hairs grow later.

steps.title: The signs of an אילונית
steps.stepSummary: An אילונית has no breasts and has pain during relations. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that her lower belly is not shaped like other women's. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds that her voice is deep.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are her signs: she has no breasts, and she has pain during relations. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: her lower abdomen is not shaped like other women's. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: her voice is deep, so you cannot tell if she is a woman or a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists the physical signs of an אילונית, just as it did for the סריס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sign shows that her body did not develop the way a woman's normally does. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's voice sign matches his voice sign for the סריס in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Thick or deep, said of a voice

steps.whatToRemember: A סריס and an אילונית are defined the same way: reaching twenty without two hairs. Each one also has a list of physical signs.

phrases.english: And these are her signs:
anyone who does not have breasts,
and has difficulty during relations.
phrases.notes: He means she feels pain during relations.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לָהּ שִׁיפּוּלֵי מֵעַיִם כְּנָשִׁים.
phrases.english: anyone whose lower abdomen is not like that of other women.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
anyone whose voice is deep,
so that one cannot tell whether she is a woman or a man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the signs of the אילונית defined in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The signs of an אילונית: no breasts, pain during relations, an undeveloped lower abdomen, and a deep voice.

steps.title: How many signs make someone a סריס
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says a man is a סריס only if all the signs are present. רבי יוחנן says even one sign is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about the signs of a סריס. רב הונא said: only if all of them are present. רבי יוחנן said: even with just one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת between two אמוראים about the list of signs from the ברייתא. The question is whether all the signs are needed, or whether one is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave many signs but never said how many are needed. רב הונא is strict about labeling someone a סריס and requires all of them. רבי יוחנן says any single sign is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Only once all of them are present

phrases.english: It was stated: the signs of a eunuch,

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ כּוּלָּם.
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: only once all of them are present.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּאֶחָד מֵהֶן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: even with one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the list of signs from the ברייתא is applied.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: all the signs are required. רבי יוחנן: one sign is enough.

steps.title: Where the two sides really argue
steps.stepSummary: If the man has grown two hairs in his beard, everyone agrees all the signs are needed. They argue only when he has not grown them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he grew two hairs in his beard, everyone agrees that all the signs are needed. They argue only where he did not grow them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the מחלוקת from Step 15 to one specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beard hairs are a strong sign that he is developing normally, so one other sign cannot cancel them out. The argument between רב הונא and רבי יוחנן applies only to a man with no beard hairs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This narrowing sets up the question in Step 17 about רב נחמן.

phrases.english: Where he grew two hairs in the beard,
everyone agrees
that it requires all of them.
Where they argue is when he did not grow them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּהֵבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת בַּזָּקָן כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the מחלוקת of Step 15 to a man without beard hairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With beard hairs, all signs are needed according to everyone. The מחלוקת is only about a man without beard hairs.

steps.title: Does רבה בר אבוה's check on רב נחמן follow רב הונא?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה told the רבנן to check whether רב נחמן gave off steam before he would give him his daughter. Checking a further sign seems to follow רב הונא, who requires all the signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רבה בר אבוה told the רבנן: check רב נחמן, and if his body gives off steam, I will give him my daughter. Whose view is this? It must be רב הונא's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses a story to challenge רבי יוחנן's view, as it was narrowed in Step 16. It argues that the story seems to fit only רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that רב נחמן had no beard, so he already showed one sign. According to רבי יוחנן, one sign would already make him a סריס, so there would be nothing left to check. Since רבה בר אבוה still checked another sign, it looks like he held רב הונא's view that all the signs are needed.

phrases.english: But that which he said to them,
Rabba bar Avuh to the Sages:
Examine Rav Naḥman,
phrases.notes: He means: look at him when he bathes, to check the steam sign from Step 12.

phrases.english: if his flesh gives off steam,
I will give him my daughter.
In accordance with whom? With Rav Huna!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a story to test the מחלוקת as it was narrowed in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that one sign is enough when there are no beard hairs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A beardless רב נחמן already had one sign. Checking another sign makes sense only if all the signs are needed, which is רב הונא's view.

steps.title: רב נחמן had a thin beard
steps.stepSummary: No, רב נחמן had wisps of a beard. That is a case where everyone agrees all the signs are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. רב נחמן had a thin beard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining that רב נחמן did have some beard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב נחמן had beard hairs, his case falls under Step 16, where everyone agrees all the signs are needed. So checking the steam sign fits רבי יוחנן's view too, and the story proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Wisps of a beard, a thin beard

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא needs all the signs, and רבי יוחנן needs only one. That מחלוקת applies only to a man without beard hairs. If he has beard hairs, everyone agrees all the signs are needed.

phrases.english: No, Rav Naḥman
had wisps of a beard.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, רַב נַחְמָן סִיכֵּי דִיקְנָא הַוְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן had no beard, so checking another sign must follow רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן had some beard, so all agree that all the signs are needed, and the story fits רבי יוחנן too.

steps.title: The סריס is listed alongside the אילונית, so both are born that way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and notes that the סריס is taught like the אילונית. Just as an אילונית is that way from Heaven, the סריס here must also be one born that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: A סריס does not do חליצה or יבום, and the same goes for an אילונית. Since the משנה puts the סריס together with the אילונית, we learn: just as an אילונית is that way from Heaven, so too the סריס here is one who is that way from Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and reads a hint from how it groups its cases. Because the סריס sits right next to the אילונית, it must be the same kind: born that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אילונית is never made that way by people. She is always born that way, so it is בידי שמים. By listing the two together, the משנה shows that its סריס is also a סריס חמה (born that way), not one who was injured by a person.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who cannot have children
A woman who cannot have children
By the hand of Heaven: born that way

phrases.english: A sexually underdeveloped man does not perform ḥalitza or enter levirate marriage,
and similarly a sexually underdeveloped woman, etc.
It teaches the underdeveloped man similar to the underdeveloped woman:
just as the underdeveloped woman is by the hand of Heaven,
so too the underdeveloped man is by the hand of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the סריס and אילונית and their signs (steps 8-18) and goes back to a line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סריס in the משנה who does not do חליצה or יבום is a סריס חמה, born that way.

steps.title: This unnamed משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the unnamed משנה matches רבי עקיבא. He says a סריס made that way by people is like any man for חליצה and יבום, but one born that way is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this unnamed משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who said: if he was made that way by people, yes, he does חליצה and יבום. If he was made that way by Heaven, no.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the last step, the גמרא names whose opinion this משנה follows: רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא splits the סריס into two kinds. A סריס אדם was injured by a person and still counts for חליצה and יבום. A סריס חמה was born that way and does not count. Our משנה only leaves out the one born that way, which is exactly רבי עקיבא's split.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed teaching, with no name attached
By the hands of man: caused by a person or injury

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's סריס who does not do חליצה or יבום is the one born that way. This follows רבי עקיבא: a סריס made that way by people still does חליצה and יבום.

phrases.english: And the unattributed view is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva,
who said: by the hands of man, yes,
phrases.notes: He means: such a man counts as a regular man and does חליצה and יבום.

phrases.english: by the hand of Heaven, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 19's reading: the משנה's author is רבי עקיבא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The unnamed משנה follows רבי עקיבא: only a סריס born that way is excluded from חליצה and יבום.

steps.title: Reading the משנה: she is disqualified because her יבם lived with her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about a סריס who did חליצה. It infers that the disqualification comes from her יבם living with her, which would mean another man would not disqualify her. This sets up a question.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: A סריס who did חליצה with his יבמה did not disqualify her (but if he lived with her, he did). The reason is that he lived with her. That suggests that if a different man did, she would not be disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and draws an inference from its wording. It is setting up the next move, which will question this inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says she is disqualified only when the סריס, her יבם, lived with her. By focusing on him, the משנה seems to say it is only because it was him. So another man would not cause this. That sounds surprising, so the גמרא is preparing to look at it more closely.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified her (here: from marrying a כהן)
He lived with her as husband and wife
But another man, no: an inference from the wording

phrases.english: A eunuch who performed ḥalitza with his yevama
did not disqualify her, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה line continues: but if he lived with her, he did disqualify her from marrying a כהן.

phrases.english: The reason is that he had relations with her,
but another man, no,

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דִּבְעָלָהּ הוּא, הָא אַחֵר — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, a new topic separate from steps 19-20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading the משנה closely: her disqualification comes from her יבם living with her, which suggests another man would not disqualify her.
